statement: For a countable tower of continuous equivariant surjections, H1_cts(G,lim P_n) -> lim H1_cts(G,P_n) is surjective. It is bijective for compact Hausdorff coefficient groups, and for finite-dimensional rational nilpotent BCH groups with continuous linear algebraic actions and surjective Lie transition maps. The twisted H0 obstruction vanishes by compactness in the first case and the Mittag-Leffler property in the second. A noncompact pro-discrete counterexample has all finite-stage H1 trivial but limit H1=Z2/Z.
where_proved: sections/F.tex, F.15; exact finite certificates in code/g_f_limit.py and code/g_f_limit_results.json
depends_on: Compactness and finite intersection property, with the argument given in full
manuscript_passages: Section 51, scans 173 and 178: successive study of splittings
notes: This removes the representative/stabilizer obstruction previously listed in F.12 for compact pro-l towers and the specified rational BCH towers. It does not evaluate their finite-stage twisted H1/H2 groups or local conditions. The pro-discrete counterexample is G=Z2, P_n=Z_disc plus Z/2^n, t(a,b)=(a,b+ta); its nonzero limit cocycle is t -> (0,t/3). No claim is made that this counterexample is the particular arithmetic realization of V. No compactness of rational-point groups and no identification of a full profinite group with its nilpotent completion are assumed.
